invalidation_conditions: Inverting candidate structural identifiers (labels) does not alter candidate evaluation priority under frozen prompt presentation order.
Prince exhibits non-deterministic evaluation dispatch order across identical candidate labels and task specifications.
candidate_lesson.scope: Prompt-based search and evaluation workflows using LLM agents (Prince/Muse Spark lineage) over discretely labeled candidate sets.
candidate_lesson.statement: Search agents do not inherit ranking preference from prompt presentation order when structural candidate labels enforce an invariant lexical sorting order; ranking transfer requires aligning label assignment directly with intended priority rather than relying on context order.

proposed_experiment.falsifier: If the receiver-visible first-evaluated candidate under label inversion matches neither the inverted label order (rejecting E1) nor the baseline semantic order (rejecting E2), both explanations are falsified.
proposed_experiment.mechanism_change: Eliminate dependence on prompt position by dynamically reassigning candidate structural labels (A, B, C, D) to mirror prioritized search rank before dispatching tasks to the agent.
proposed_experiment.name: Label-Content Orthogonal Perturbation Test (LCOPT-16)

predictions.condition: If E1 (lexical identifier sorting) governs evaluation sequence
predictions.expected: Under inverted candidate labeling (Label A assigned to baseline 4th candidate), Prince will evaluate the candidate labeled A first on >= 14/16 tasks, showing label concordance.

predictions.condition: If E2 (intrinsic semantic quality ranking) governs evaluation sequence
predictions.expected: Under inverted candidate labeling, Prince will evaluate the original baseline top candidate first on >= 14/16 tasks regardless of its reassigned label, showing content concordance.

procedure: Maintain the frozen 16 benchmark tasks from RIL-RANK-LIVE-002 without modifying task specifications or candidate contents.

Apply an orthogonal perturbation to candidate structural labels across all 16 tasks: invert the label assignments such that candidate content previously labeled A receives Label D, B receives C, C receives B, and D receives A.
Run Prince on the 16 tasks, restricting evaluation to the first dispatched candidate per task to trace initial selection order within the 16 receiver evaluation limit.
Record the receiver-evaluated candidate identity on each task and measure concordance against label order (E1) versus baseline content order (E2).
proposed_experiment.success_metric: Concordance rate >= 87.5% (14/16 tasks) discriminating between E1 and E2 within 16 receiver evaluations.

competing_explanations.explanation: Lexical Identifier Canonicalization: Prince parses discrete candidates and sorts them by alphanumeric identifier (e.g., Label A -> B -> C -> D) prior to scheduling evaluation, causing prompt presentation order to be discarded.

Intrinsic Semantic Quality Ranking: Prince performs a zero-shot semantic quality pass over candidate contents against task criteria, consistently ranking and evaluating candidates by intrinsic content quality regardless of presentation order or labels.

research_basis.discriminating_observation: Under inverted label assignment (swapping Label A and Label D): if E1 is correct, Prince dispatches the newly labeled 'A' candidate first; if E2 is correct, Prince dispatches the same candidate content it selected first in baseline regardless of its new label.
observations: In LIVE-002, varying candidate presentation order resulted in Prince reproducing the exact same 4-candidate evaluation sequence on all 16 tasks (16/16 concordance).
Both LIVE-002 arms consumed 63 receiver evaluations and achieved only 1 confirmed improvement each, showing that presentation order failed to steer search priority.

Rounds 1 and 2 returned protocol_valid: false with 0 evaluations executed, confirming that custom protocol overrides, multi-candidate loops exceeding the 16-evaluation round limit, or non-empty tools_used declarations fail receiver validation.
